statement: No stamina and no "body" number exist in any code or data, so the energy, stamina and health loop Orb defined for Alpha is a plan only.
evidence: git grep -i stamina 8901d351 -- sim render ui net data audio: 0 hits
cost_basis: estimate from the project's rates: about 1M tokens per director session (docs/ep/proposals/controller-vision.md:163) and 0.4M per hash window (docs/ep/proposals/terrain-globe-plan.md:321); a design page, sim, director costs, HUD and fighter read, QA re-baseline, about 4 to 6 sessions
risk: The plan itself names a runaway (the fighter landing blows gets stronger while the one hit gets worse injuries); QA's count of how often the fighter who falls behind first still wins shows it early.
orb_question: How much of the stamina, energy and body loop must be in Alpha? Recommendation: the whole loop as shared rules with per-fighter numbers in data, switched on only after QA's comeback measurement.

statement: No single written page states the model: it is spread over six design pages, the oldest still a proposal that disagrees with the code on the brink, and none covers stamina.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable; one page by one director
risk: A page written before the body and knockout questions are answered will be rewritten.

statement: Energy's own numbers (start, cap, regain, charge rate, hit gain, guard drain and the older costs) are literals in code, shared by every fighter, not data.
cost_basis: estimate from 0.1M a file touched and 0.4M a hash window (docs/ep/proposals/terrain-globe-plan.md:321); about eight files plus gates and one window
risk: A moved number that changes value by rounding moves every golden; the parity gate shows it at once.

statement: The "one energy model" is off in the data on main and in both played builds, and is on in Orb's build only through a code patch the page tool writes, so main does not describe the game Orb played.
cost_basis: one data flip in a hash window, 0.4M by docs/ep/proposals/terrain-globe-plan.md:321
risk: Turning it on in data moves the golden and every replay; a desktop build made without the page tool would silently play with the model off until then.

statement: The backburnered hero and villain meters still change damage, energy regain, beam contests and where the computer leads the fight in every match, with no readout in the normal HUD.
cost_basis: estimate from 0.1M a file touched and 0.4M a hash window (docs/ep/proposals/terrain-globe-plan.md:321), plus a QA balance batch
risk: The Protagonist's only comeback rule hangs on his meter, so switching the meters off without folding it in tilts every match; QA's win-rate batch shows it.
orb_question: The backburnered meters: switch off, fold in, or retire? Recommendation: keep the comeback as a rule for every fighter, zero every other effect in data now, remove the code after Alpha.

statement: The tool X-15 names does not measure X-15: the two-fighter ratchet counts four spellings of "exactly two fighters" and says nothing about fighter-specific code.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable; the existing ratchet is 84 lines
risk: X-15 could be signed off on a passing ratchet while fighter-specific code remains.

statement: A health bar can still be put on screen: F2 swaps in the old overlay with a hit-point bar and MENACE or ANGUISH bars.
risk: The overlay also carries the take-over prompt and the performance readout, so removing it whole could drop those.

statement: No record shows that a player can read their own health, energy or readiness from the fighter at speed; the only energy readout found is the corner plate.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable; one clip-based read test
risk: Outside testers may not know they are near defeat or out of energy; a blind read test on saved clips shows it before they play.

statement: The HUD's power pip is computed at 25 per tier while the data's thresholds are 35, 65 and 100, so it reads full before a transformation is ready.
risk: None beyond a HUD still to re-check.

statement: Body marks only grow to the worst stage reached and never fade, so the fighter cannot show recovery or the easing of injuries Orb wants from a new form.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable; needs the look gate's side-by-side
risk: Marks that fade may read as a glitch; the look gate's side-by-side shows it.

statement: A new kind of meter cannot be added as data: the loader accepts only the two backburnered meter names.
The old hit-point number is still tracked beside the wounds as a second health value, and QA's tools and three director files still read it.
cost_basis: estimate from 0.1M a file touched and 0.4M a hash window (docs/ep/proposals/terrain-globe-plan.md:321)
risk: QA's damage readings are built on it, so removing it before a replacement breaks their batches.
orb_question: Is "body" a new number, or the old hidden hit-point number renamed and reused? Recommendation: reuse it, so one deep health number sits behind the four body parts.

statement: Several damage numbers are code constants shared by all fighters: the stance table, combo growth, the charging penalty and five pinned wound values.
Render and content still key some looks and kit rows on a fighter's id, name or the words "hero" and "villain", so a third fighter is not proven to need data and art only outside the sim.
risk: A third fighter would silently wear a default look; a copied-fighter render run shows it.

statement: The Protagonist's own forms are off in data on main and in both played builds and the rival has no forms file, so "reaching new forms" is the shared four-tier ladder for both.
cost_basis: counted under the transformations area (X-04), not here
risk: The energy and stamina loop is meant to encourage reaching forms, so it cannot be tuned until the form question is settled.

statement: The rule that makes a match always end is off on main and on in Orb's build, so with hit points no longer ending a match, main's data alone does not guarantee an end.
cost_basis: one data flip in a hash window, 0.4M by docs/ep/proposals/terrain-globe-plan.md:321
risk: A build made from main without the page tool could run a match with no end.

statement: Leftovers of hiding still sit in the energy and health code (faster regain and healing while hidden, x1.5 ambush damage), inert because no fighter can hide.
risk: None while no fighter can hide.

statement: Health is injury-based with no bar: four body regions with stages, and only a finisher ends a match.
The normal HUD has no health bar and draws nothing over the fighters.
Health shows on the fighter: marks by body region and stage, a sag and slower get-ups toward the brink, and an aura flicker.
A third fighter built from data alone plays a match in the sim, checked in CI.
The two-fighter ratchet runs and passes at 365 against a baseline of 365, in CI.
Wound and ladder numbers live in data with a per-fighter override the loader supports, and the stage penalties read that data.
